title: Natural selection preserves favourable and destroys injurious variations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection preserves favourable and destroys injurious variations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because more individuals are born than can survive, individuals with any advantage, however slight, have the best chance of surviving and reproducing, while injurious variations are eliminated; this preservation of favourable and rejection of injurious variations is natural selection.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This preservation of favourable variations and the rejection of injurious variations, I call Natural Selection.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IV, “Natural Selection”; section “Natural Selection: its power compared with man’s selection, its power on characters of trifling importance, its power at all ages and on both sexes”. Scope: all organisms in nature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch04-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern quantitative genetics makes the mechanism explicit and many open studies measure selection directly. The all-organism scope and context dependence prevent full resolution from existing datasets.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate associations between heritable trait or allele values and survival and reproductive success across populations. Consistently positive selection differentials for advantageous variants and negative differentials for harmful variants support the mechanism; absent or reversed fitness effects refute it in tested systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Advantage is environment-dependent and risks being defined circularly by survival.

Available longitudinal fitness data cover a small fraction of organisms.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Superfecundity and the removal of deleterious alleles are measurable, and open demographic and genomic resources support standard tests of both. The preservation of favourable variation is only weakly separable from the definition of a favourable variant, so many outcomes are compatible with the wording either as a mechanism or as a tautology. Existing data therefore test pieces of the statement in a few well-studied organisms rather than the universal process as named.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the distribution of fitness effects from allele-frequency spectra, and estimate surplus offspring from life tables. Purifying selection would be confirmed if deleterious alleles are systematically rarer than neutral alleles and if populations produce far more offspring than survive; the differential-success clause would be refuted if fitness effects did not predict frequency change. The sentence that names this process natural selection has no separate measurement.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Life tables show excess births without identifying which heritable differences selection retains.

Population-genomic samples are concentrated in humans and model organisms.

An advantage defined as higher survival or reproduction makes the central clause close to a definition of fitness.
